content: 1. Materials that are thermally unstable and capable of undergoing a strongly exothermic decomposition without the involvement of oxygen (air) are classified as self-reactive materials. These materials are not influenced by artificially changing variables such as pressure or density, nor by the addition of accelerants. Certain exclusions to this classification are outlined under 49 CFR. Self-reactive materials are categorized into a generic system consisting of seven types, and specific materials are assigned to these types based on the procedures described in the regulations. 2. Metal powders that can ignite and react along the entire length of a sample within 10 minutes or less, when tested according to the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, are also included in this classification. Additionally, materials that propagate a reaction at a rate of at least 87 inches per second under the same testing conditions are considered hazardous. 3. Pyrophoric materials are substances, either liquid or solid, that can ignite spontaneously within five minutes of exposure to air, even in small quantities and without an external ignition source. This behavior is determined through testing in accordance with the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria. 4. Self-heating materials are those that, upon contact with air and without any external energy supply, are prone to self-heating. This property is also evaluated using the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria. 5. Dangerous when wet materials are substances that, upon contact with water, can either become spontaneously flammable or release flammable or toxic gases at a rate exceeding 1 liter per kilogram of the material per hour. This classification is determined through testing as specified in the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria.
